conviction_note: Peers that printed after Oscar last spoke (Elevance 10-21, Centene 10-27, Molina 10-21) all describe ACA H2 cost and retention at or better than expected, and Oscar's own guide leaves an implied H2 operating loss of $293-493m that management said was not taking full credit for favorability, so the print and guide likely beat (findings sum +0.7); but the stock ran +16.7% in five sessions and +9% on the day before the print to a 52-week high, call open interest dominates, and the last beat-and-raise (2026-08-06) was sold -11.86%, so p_up sits at 51 and the scaled number (+0.19 on a 9.5-point move) is far smaller than the fundamental read.
bar: Q3 2026 consensus EPS a loss of about $0.22-0.25 (Chartmill -0.22 https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/OSCR/estimates ; Benzinga -0.25 https://kr.benzinga.com/quote/OSCR/earnings-forecasts ; Earnings Whispers -0.27; Investing.com preview of 2026-11-04 carries -0.14 on $4.69B https://ng.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/oscar-health-earnings-on-deck-can-insurer-sustain-profit-93CH-2783576), revenue $4.69-4.82B. Estimates disagree (-0.11 to -0.27), so the quarterly bar is soft; the firmer bar is the company's FY2026 guide from the 2026-09-16 8-K: earnings from operations $600-800m, MLR 81.0-82.0%, revenue $18.7-19.0B, SG&A 15.6-16.1% (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001568651/000156865126000074/oscr-20260916.htm). H1 2026 EFO was $1,092.7m (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001568651/000156865126000066/oscarhealthsecondquarter20.htm), so the guide implies an H2 operating loss of $293-493m. print_vs_bar_pct is on revenue. Note: the sweep row's 'already_in_the_wire' item (Q2 MLR 91.1%, $230m loss) is the Q2 2025 comparative column, not Q2 2026.
positioning_check: Short interest 18.29M shares at the 2026-10-15 settlement, about 3.7 days to cover, on 273.5M shares outstanding (~6.7% of shares out, ~8-9% of float given 22.6% insider ownership), up from 16.45M / 2.7 days at 2026-09-30 (https://massive.com/quote/oscr, read 2026-11-04). Not a crowded short. Baseline skew_25d -3.35 vol points (upside paid), put/call OI 0.38 (call-heavy), event-implied move 9.62%, straddle 10.15%. Tape: spot 35.57 at the 52-week high, run_up_5d +16.7%, run_up_20d +8.1%, +9.2% intraday on 2026-11-04 from a $32.41 close with no identified catalyst; YTD about +146%. Sell-side consensus Hold, average target $34.90 (below spot) per MarketBeat 2026-11-04.

findings.finding: Elevance (Q3 call 2026-10-21) said its individual ACA business beat expectations: the H2 cost ramp as members reach deductibles is 'coming through more slowly than expected', it retained more ACA members than planned (now >=1.2M year-end vs ~1.0M expected) and it expects a modestly higher full-year ACA operating margin; Oscar's guide and the Street's Q3 loss of ~$0.22-0.25 both assume the seasonal H2 MLR rise Oscar's CEO described in August ('continue to trend higher quarterly').
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 (MLR far below plan) +10.59%; Q2 2026 MLR 79.2% vs guide 82.4-83.4% with a $250m raise sold -11.86% on churn worries; Q3 2025 smaller-than-expected loss -2.76%. Beats on MLR have paid twice and been sold twice.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: Oscar is +16.7% in five sessions and at a 52-week high. If fully priced, consensus Q3 EPS would have moved toward breakeven after 10-21; the estimates still sit at -0.22 to -0.27 at most aggregators, and one dated 11-04 is -0.14, so some revisions may have started. A peer print landing after the company last spoke (Oscar's investor day 2026-09-16) is the case where consensus goes stale.
findings.independence: Elevance 10-Q language 'improved performance in our Individual ACA' (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001156039/000115603926000071/elv-20260930.htm). Centene, a separate source, points the same way (next finding). Proxy: Elevance's ACA book is a different mix (Blue states, fewer new members) than Oscar's.

findings.finding: Centene's Q3 2026 release (2026-10-27) says the consolidated HBR benefited from a lower Marketplace HBR 'resulting from improved pricing and risk transfer reflecting the acuity of the Marketplace membership', Marketplace is 'on track', commercial HBR fell to 89.0% from 89.9%, and Marketplace membership slipped only 2.6% in the quarter (3,494,700 at 6-30 to 3,403,300 at 9-30); Centene raised its FY adjusted EPS floor to >$5.20.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Oscar has traded with Centene's marketplace read: in 2025 Centene's marketplace warning and Molina's warning took Oscar down with them. Oscar's own risk-adjustment surprises: Q2 2025 guidance cut on market morbidity (sold), Q2 2026 +$160m 2025 RA favorability with raised guide (sold -11.86%).
findings.why_not_priced: Risk transfer is zero-sum across the market: Oscar is a net payer ($4.85B net RA payable at 6-30) and if Centene's acuity is higher relative to the market, Oscar's transfer could be larger, which is the ambiguity that leaves the read-through unpriced. The 'improved pricing' half and the shallow Q3 membership decline are direct read-throughs on the two things Oscar's August sell-off was about (pricing adequacy and H2 churn). Partly priced through the 5-day run.
findings.independence: Different company and document from the Elevance finding. Molina (separate) said marketplace MCR 92.5% 'in line with normal seasonality' (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001179929/000117992926000042/moh3q26_er.htm). Proxy: risk transfer can cut the other way for Oscar.

findings.finding: Molina's Q3 2026 release (2026-10-21) put Marketplace MCR at 92.5%, 'in line with normal seasonality and the Company's expectations', and reaffirmed FY adjusted EPS >= $5.25: no ACA cost surprise from the third public exchange carrier.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In October 2025 a Molina marketplace warning took Oscar and Centene down the same day (https://www.benzinga.com/markets/earnings/25/10/48387644/centene-and-oscar-health-stocks-sink-after-molina-warning); this year there was no warning.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: an absence of a warning is public. Filed small because it removes the downside tail that hit Oscar a year ago rather than adding upside.
findings.independence: Same direction as Elevance and Centene, separate document. Molina's marketplace is small (267k members) and shrinking, so it is a weak proxy.

findings.finding: Oscar's own FY2026 guide (raised twice: 8-6 to EFO $500-700m, 9-16 to $600-800m, MLR 81.0-82.0%) against H1 EFO of $1,092.7m implies an H2 operating loss of $293-493m, and on the Q2 call the CFO said 'we have not taken full credit for that favorability in our outlook' (2026 risk-adjustment morbidity signal booked only in small part) and 'there's more tailwinds than headwinds'; with peers reporting slower H2 cost ramps, a third raise or a firm top-of-range at the Q3 print is the likely guidance outcome.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance raises: 2026-08-06 +$250m raise sold -11.86%; 2026-09-16 investor day +$100m raise followed by price-target hikes (Barclays $49, Raymond James $42). 2026-05-06 reaffirm with big beat +10.59%. A raise is not sufficient on this name.
findings.why_not_priced: A raise is partly expected given the run to a 52-week high; what is not in the consensus is its size: the Q3 consensus loss of ~$0.22-0.25 times ~260M shares is ~-$60m, which leaves Q4 carrying most of the implied H2 loss, and the held-back 2026 RA favorability is unquantified. If the Street had priced a large raise, the average target ($34.90) would not sit below spot.
findings.independence: Guide figures from Oscar's 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001568651/000156865126000074/oscr-20260916.htm) and H1 figures from the Q2 8-K; the 'not taken full credit' quote is from the call transcript and summarized independently at https://actuary.info/insights/oscar-health-q2-2026-aca-risk-adjustment-accrual-mlr-morbidity. Shares its peer support with the Elevance/Centene findings, but this finding is about the guide, not the quarter.

findings.finding: Membership attrition is the line the August sell-off was blamed on: the Q2 10-Q estimated 250,000-300,000 members could be retroactively disenrolled under CMS program-integrity rules (of 2,963,002 at 6-30), and the CEO said churn would run 'closer to twice' the prior 1-2% assumption; Q3 effectuated membership will show the size of it, and any 2027 enrollment commentary under expired enhanced subsidies lands on the same call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-08-06: a Stephens analyst cited H2 attrition as the probable reason the stock fell 13% intraday (-11.86% close) on a record quarter and raised guide (https://parameter.io/oscar-health-oscr-stock-plunges-9-despite-crushing-q2-earnings-expectations/).
findings.why_not_priced: The disclosure is public, so the risk is known; what is unknown is the Q3 number. Sized small and net of the peer evidence: Elevance retained more than planned and Centene's marketplace fell only 2.6% in Q3, which shrinks this negative. Management called it 'a timing move that doesn't impact revenue'.
findings.independence: Offset by Elevance (better retention) and Centene (shallow Q3 decline). Same 10-Q/call as the guidance finding but a different line (membership, not earnings).

findings.finding: Into the print the stock is at its 52-week high ($35.57, +16.7% in 5 sessions, +9.2% on 2026-11-04 alone from a $32.41 close, YTD ~+146%) with no identified company catalyst, call-dominated open interest (P/C 0.38) and upside skew; the last print with a big beat and raise (2026-08-06) fell 11.86%, and sell-side average target $34.90 is below spot.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Last eight reactions: -11.86, +10.59, +1.74, -2.76, +3.76, +7.93, +30.22, +3.08; 6 of 8 up, median |move| 5.84%. The August -11.86% came after a run-up into a beat.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself: a +9% day before the print with no named catalyst raises the bar the release must clear. The option market leans the other way (skew -3.35, upside paid), which is why this is sized below the implied move; short interest ~8-9% of float and 3.7 days to cover (rising) is not crowded but adds some squeeze fuel if the guide is strong.
findings.independence: Price data also at https://massive.com/quote/oscr (2026-11-04: +9.23%, 52-week range $10.69-36.16) and Investing.com's 52-week-high note (https://in.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/oscar-health-stock-hits-52week-high-at-3563-usd-93CH-5679509). The baseline's own run_up_5d (+16.7%) is the same fact.

findings.finding: For 2027 Oscar filed an average 26.9% rate increase on renewing plans (GA filing, March-2026 in-force basis; 33.9% in Arizona, the highest carrier request there) against a KFF market median near 14-15%, and is expanding to 713 counties in 21 states (+24%) while Centene exits Delaware and New Hampshire and Cigna drops ~369k exchange members; open enrollment began 2026-11-01, so the Q3 call is the first chance for early 2027 color.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q3 2025 call that first framed 2026 ('return to profitability') was followed by a -2.76% day; 2026 rate-hike news (28%) in 2025 drove a +6.7% day (https://rallies.ai/news/oscar-health-plans-28-rate-hike-after-37-revenue-growth-shares-jump-67).
findings.why_not_priced: Filings and the footprint are public; how management frames 2027 margin vs growth is not. A rate request far above the market median protects margin but risks share, so the sign depends on the commentary; sized small.
findings.independence: Footprint and competitor exits from Becker's (https://www.beckerspayer.com/payer/aca/how-insurers-aca-footprints-are-changing-in-2027/); market median from KFF via https://www.bioxconomy.com/pricing-and-contracting/aca-insurers-seek-14-hike-for-2027-coverage.

findings.finding: Insiders sold $79.3m over the 12 months to 2026-11-04 (co-founder Schlosser $68.8m, CFO $7.9m), with 10b5-1 Form 144s through August-September and a Schedule 13D/A on 2026-09-18; the CEO bought $11.9m in April 2026.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No observed reaction to these sales; the stock rose through them.
findings.why_not_priced: Public and mostly pre-arranged plans; filed only because a judge may weigh supply from a 13D holder differently. Near zero.
findings.independence: EDGAR filing index (https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001568651&type=&dateb=&owner=include&count=40) shows the 144s, Form 4s and the 2026-09-18 13D/A.

outside_window.finding: 2027 ACA open-enrollment volume under expired enhanced subsidies (OE runs 2026-11-01 to 2027-01-15 on HealthCare.gov) and final effectuation; CMS snapshots come after the window.
Full 2026 benefit-year risk-adjustment transfer report (CMS, ~June 2027), which settles how much of the held-back morbidity favorability is real.

searched_and_found_nothing: A named catalyst for the +9.2% move on 2026-11-04 (MarketBeat, Investing.com and massive.com report the move with no cause; no Oscar 8-K since 2026-09-16 on EDGAR)
A CMS 2027 open-enrollment early snapshot (none published by 2026-11-04)
A second Wakely 2026 market-morbidity update after the July white paper
Oscar 8-K or preannouncement in October 2026 (EDGAR shows only Form 4s since 9-22)
Unusual options flow headlines for November 2026 (only older items found)

baseline_tension: The fundamental evidence (three peers clean or better, a guide that management called conservative) agrees with the upside skew and call-heavy positioning, which is exactly why it is probably largely in a price that rose 16.7% in five sessions and 9% the day before; the run-up and the August beat-and-sell reaction cut against it.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a reaction; this name sold its last beat-and-raise): peer read-through findings trimmed, Elevance 1.2 to 1.0, Centene 1.0 to 0.8, Molina 0.3 to 0.2; p_up held at 51 rather than raised.

Lesson 7 (positioning; sign against skew needs a reason): the run-up/positioning negative cut from -2.0 to -1.8 because the option skew (-3.35) leans up and short interest (~8-9% of float, 3.7 days, rising) adds modest squeeze fuel.

Lesson 6 (verify the bar): Q3 EPS estimates disagree (-0.11 to -0.27), so the guidance finding is sized against the company's FY guide, which is sourced; no further cap applied beyond the existing small sizes.

Lesson 5 (proxy vs document): peer findings kept as filed proxies (peer prints after the company last spoke is the pattern that has paid); 2027 finding 0.5 to 0.4 and insider -0.2 to -0.1 as low-information items.
Lesson 3 (caveat reaches the number): the membership negative is sized net of Elevance/Centene retention evidence; abs_move_pct and p_up unchanged.
